q: The plan says the wire set is five positions, but `git grep -n '"omp"' -- packages/{coding-agent,catalog,utils,tui}/src` finds several more bare-literal wire values this item does not touch. Two of them are serious and are NOT display strings: `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/auth/stencil.kdl:13` (`client-id "omp"` — the OAuth client id registered at the Stencil issuer; renaming it breaks Stencil login, and per AGENTS.md it lives in KDL so a TS constant cannot simply be substituted) and `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/auth/openai-codex.kdl:12` (`originator "omp"`). Non-KDL extras: `packages/coding-agent/src/cli/git-tui/avatar.ts:50` (`"User-Agent": "omp"` on the GitHub API), `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/report-tool-issue.ts:441` (`agent: { name: "omp" }` in a POSTed grievance body), `packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/omp-protocol.ts:28` (`readonly scheme = "omp"` — the omp:// URL scheme). HUMAN DECISION: does the milestone owner want these folded into W1's wire set, assigned to a later work item, or explicitly recorded as do-not-touch? Do NOT silently add them — the plan explicitly forbids a sixth site — and do NOT silently leave them either, or W7's `sed` and W8b's display-token sweep become the thing that decides. My recommendation is a separate, explicit work item, because the two KDL ones need a KDL-level fix that this item must not attempt.

`packages/catalog/src/wire/codex.ts:52` is declared READ-ONLY by this item, but its real source is the writable KDL rule `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/auth/openai-codex.kdl:12`. The compiled `rules.json` is committed. So a later `sed`-style pass over the KDL tree, or a `bun run gen:compat` after an unrelated KDL edit, can move this value with no TypeScript diff at all. HUMAN DECISION: who owns the invariant that the OpenAI originator stays "omp", and does it need a test before W7 runs? This is a real hole in the plan's own framing, not a hypothetical.

The DAP site (`dap/session.ts:1465-1466`) has no direct test and I recommend not building a harness for it. HUMAN DECISION: accept transitive coverage (all five sites read one constant, and four goldens plus the new constant test pin its value), or spend the effort on a `vi.spyOn(DapClient, "spawn")` harness? The DAP `clientID`/`clientName` pair is the only one of the five whose consumer is a third-party debug adapter rather than an in-repo subsystem, so it is the one where a silent break is least likely to be noticed by the maintainers themselves.

`packages/coding-agent/src/hindsight/settings.ts:172` registers `cfgHindsightRetainContext` with `default: "omp"` — the same bank-namespace identity as `bank.ts:29`, but a separate persisted config key with its own default. Five test files carry `retainContext: "omp"` as a FIXTURE INPUT (hindsight-bank.test.ts:55, hindsight-conversation-timestamps.test.ts:35, hindsight-mm-cache-stability.test.ts:34, hindsight-retention-cache.test.ts:27, memory-tools.test.ts:63). HUMAN DECISION: is this the same wire identity (in which case it should also read WIRE_NAME, changing an existing default and its persisted value) or an independent user-facing setting default (in which case it stays)? I have left it out of W1 because changing a registered setting's default is a behaviour change, not a refactor, and that is W3's territory. Flagging it because five test fixtures currently hardcode it and the next person to sweep literals will trip on it.

Do we accept the W2a / W2b split, or does the milestone owner want W2 kept as one commit that must be merged in the same PR as W7 pass 1? The split is strictly safer (it creates no window in which the canonical scope names a scope that does not exist) but it does move one line of W2 out of wave 1, which is a visible change to the plan's wave structure. A human must decide because it reorders the milestone, not just the code.

If W2b and W7 pass 1 must ship together, who owns the release gate that stops W2b from being cherry-picked alone? A CODEOWNERS entry or a CI check asserting `git grep -m1 '"name"' -- packages/utils/package.json` returns `@ultraworkers/pi-utils` whenever `CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE` is `@ultraworkers` would make the failure impossible rather than merely documented.

N17 is recorded as settled ('keep all 16 basenames') but the plan's own open-questions table still presents it as an open product decision. W2 must not resolve it either way. Confirm the plan's final position before anyone touches `PI_PACKAGE_NAMES`.

XDG blast radius: dirs.ts:360 là `const appRoot = path.join(value, APP_NAME)` và chỉ dùng XDG khi `fs.existsSync(appRoot)`. Đổi APP_NAME khiến người dùng XDG rơi về configRoot (~/.omp) vì root mới chưa tồn tại — sessions và secret-placeholder.key (dirs.ts:983) biến mất khỏi tầm tay, và secret key bị sinh lại thì giải mã secret cũ hỏng. Cần người quyết định: (a) W3 chấp nhận rủi ro vì XDG là opt-in và ít người dùng, (b) tách APP_NAME thành APP_NAME (display) + XDG_DIR_NAME (đóng băng "omp") để W3 thực sự chỉ đổi tên hiển thị, hay (c) trì hoãn W3 tới khi W6 có migration. Khuyến nghị (b): rẻ nhất và giữ đúng ý nghĩa tên hàng của W3.
Giá trị mới của APP_NAME là gì? Plan không nêu. Kỹ sư cần chốt trước khi sửa vì nó xuất hiện ở 6 file và 4 file test.
Có kéo `composer-shape-preview.ts:45` (PREVIEW_TITLE) vào W3 không? Plan bỏ sót; tôi đã đưa vào scope vì cùng package tui, cùng tính chất tên hiển thị, và test của nó đang ghim "omp".

Có kéo `relay/server.ts:55` (DEFAULT_GROUP title của tab group trình duyệt) vào W3 không? Tôi để NGOÀI scope vì đó là nhãn chrome trình duyệt, không phải tên ứng dụng — nhưng nó sẽ thành literal trùng lặp thứ 10.

Should getConfigDirCandidates() include the project-level name, or stay strictly home-scoped? This spec keeps it home-scoped and gives the project path its own pinned constant, matching W6a option (b). If the product later wants a project-level dual root too, that is W6a option (a) and it additionally requires config migrate to move project .omp directories — which are often committed to git, so migrate would have to read both and never delete.

The plan's M5 open question on the PI_*/OMP_* family (plan line 14025) is answered 'keep forever as aliases' by N16, and W4 implements exactly that for one variable. The other 149 runtime-read names in the family stay PI_-prefixed in this milestone. Confirm that is intended rather than an oversight, since the product will ship named ultraworkers with PI_-prefixed configuration vocabulary.

docs/environment-variables.md documents 100 env variables. W4 adds one row and amends one. Should the other config-adjacent variables in the family get new aliases in a later wave, or is one alias sufficient evidence of the pattern?

Should the cache be process-lifetime, or should config migrate be able to force a re-resolution in-process? With a process-lifetime cache, a migrate that moves ~/.omp to ~/.ultraworkers leaves the running process resolving to a directory that no longer exists. That is harmless for a one-shot CLI command that exits, but it should be a stated decision rather than an accident.

Should `config migrate` refuse to run while a daemon or session is live, or warn and proceed? The verified presence of `agent.db`/`history.db`/`models.db` with `-wal`/`-shm` siblings and `run/daemons/<hash>/` makes this a real corruption risk, but a hard refusal means a user with a stuck daemon cannot migrate at all. The plan does not raise it. Recommend: detect a live daemon via the existing lock surface in `packages/utils/src/file-lock.ts`, print a clear refusal naming the command that stops it, and let `--force` override. Needs a product decision before implementation.

What exactly is `MigrationOptions.oldName` at call time — the literal `".omp"`, or the previous value of `CONFIG_DIR_NAME` read before W6 flips it? The literal is correct for W5-as-shipped (W6 has not landed). But if W5 is ever backported or re-run after W6, the literal silently goes stale. Recommend capturing it as a named constant next to `CONFIG_DIR_NAME` so the relationship is explicit and greppable.

Should the XDG roots be migrated at all, given `init-xdg` is opt-in? Migrating `$XDG_*_HOME/omp` for a user who never ran `init-xdg` is a no-op because the directory does not exist, so the three-way rule absorbs it. But on a Linux box where `XDG_DATA_HOME` is set and an unrelated `omp` directory happens to live there, migrate would move a directory it did not create. Recommend requiring the old path to look like a config root (contains `agent/` or `install-id`) before proposing a move, and reporting anything else as a conflict rather than silently renaming it.

Does W5 ship with a changelog entry? The plan says changelog updates happen only when a work item asks for one, and the W5 section does not ask. This spec therefore proposes none. Confirm that is intended, since `config migrate` is a user-visible command and the M5 changelog will otherwise have no trace of it.

Should the engine live in `packages/utils` at all, or in a new `packages/coding-agent/src/config-migrate/` with the tests moved to a package that can run? The engine is dirs-shaped and depends on nothing but `node:fs`/`node:path`, and `packages/utils/src/dirs.ts` is its natural neighbour — but the placement was chosen here for the gate, and that reason should be confirmed by the reviewer rather than assumed.

Where does do_not_rename.tsv actually live? The plan's §2.3 defines it as a 17-row table but never names a file path, and scripts/rename/ does not exist yet. This spec proposes scripts/rename/do_not_rename.tsv alongside W8b's disposition.tsv. Confirm with the W7/W8b owner — a registry in the wrong place is one W7 will not read, and W7's sed pass is what makes the exclusion set load-bearing.

Should W6 wait for W4 and W5 to be used in a real release, or is 'shipped and CI-green' enough? The plan says both must have shipped AND been used in a real release. That is a calendar dependency no test can discharge, and it is the one gate that cannot be automated.

Is the string 'This project (.omp/rules)' in the omfg rules editor a literal in the controller, or derived from a constant? If literal, it correctly stays '.omp' and the user-visible label is unchanged; if it is built from a renamed constant it would drift from the on-disk path. Step 5 tells the implementer to check this, but the answer should be recorded in the commit message so a later reader knows it was deliberate.

1. BLOCKING — packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:12. priorityList feeds BOTH USER_CONFIG_BASES (line 84) and PROJECT_CONFIG_BASES (line 90) from the same `dir` value, and line 135 compares `name !== CONFIG_DIR_NAME` to decide user-source opt-in. If PROJECT_DIR_NAME is introduced and this file is untouched, the project entry in PROJECT_CONFIG_BASES silently becomes '.ultraworkers' — a project-level behaviour change hiding inside a constant rename. Recommendation: switch that one priorityList entry to PROJECT_DIR_NAME so project config keeps reading the committed .omp. This is a product decision (does the user's repo keep its committed .omp?) and must be answered by a person before merge, not inferred by the implementer. Affects: getConfigDirs('skills'|'commands'|'agents'|'hooks', {level:'project'}) and every project-level config lookup routed through it.

2. NON-BLOCKING — should the do_not_rename row for the project .omp be created by this work item or left to whichever item first creates scripts/rename/keep-list.txt? Verified: scripts/rename/ does not exist on HEAD 84cbac9, so somebody has to create it. Plan section 2.3 assigns the file to the milestone, W7 gates on it, and section 2.3's format requires a mandatory '#' reason per entry. Recommendation: W6a creates it with the single project-.omp row, appending rather than overwriting if a sibling got there first.

3. NON-BLOCKING — is a permanent divergence (CONFIG_DIR_NAME = '.ultraworkers', PROJECT_DIR_NAME = '.omp', forever) acceptable as a shipped end state, or does it need a dated follow-up? The plan's option (b) is a keep-forever decision and N14 records it as such. Worth a maintainer's explicit acknowledgement because the codebase will permanently carry two directory names, and the next person to read dirs.ts:27-40 will ask why.

4. NON-BLOCKING, environment — the coding-agent negative controls (omfg-controller.test.ts, extensions-discovery.test.ts) cannot run on this machine without `brew install ninja` followed by `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build`. Should the milestone's verification environment be provisioned once so the whole negative-control set becomes runnable, or should each spec keep declaring which of its gates are locally unrunnable? Recommend the former: the blocker has now cost every work item in this milestone a caveat, and a working addon would let the strongest signals actually fire.

AI LÀ NGƯỜI DUYỆT, DUYỆT LÚC NÀO, VÀ NẾU KHÔNG CÓ AI DUYỆT THÌ MỤC NÀY CÓ BỊ CHẶN KHÔNG? Đây là câu hỏi vận hành, và plan chỉ trả lời bằng một câu. Cụ thể: (1) AI — lịch sử git của repo này chỉ có hai tác giả, `E2E <e2e@example.com>` (7 commit) và `Tran Quang Dang <tranquangdang21@gmail.com>` (1 commit), và identity đang cấu hình là `E2E`. Vậy người duyệt là người thứ hai kia, hay chính `E2E` phải đổi identity, hay quy tắc này vô hiệu lực khi milestone chạy một mình? (2) KHI NÀO — trước khi viết dòng đầu tiên của bảng, hay sau khi viết xong? Plan nói 'không duyệt thì W8b không được sửa dòng nào trong 585 file đó', nghĩa là duyệt PHẢI xảy ra trước khi sửa mã, tức là trước khi viết bảng xong — vậy người duyệt phải theo dõi tiến trình viết bảng chứ không thể duyệt một lần lúc PR mở. (3) NẾU KHÔNG CÓ AI — câu trả lời đề xuất là KHÔNG chặn, nhưng phải ghi rõ trong PR rằng bảng tự duyệt và ai đã đọc. Lý do không nên chặn cứng: W8b là mục không quy ra ngày được, chặn nó vô điều kiện vì thiếu một người có nghĩa là milestone không bao giờ ship được phần hiển thị. Nhưng đặc tả này KHÔNG tự quyết — đó là quyết định của người đứng ngoài. Cách tôi đã cài để câu hỏi này không chỉ nằm trên giấy: `--stage=pre` kiểm `git log --format='%ae' -- scripts/rename/disposition.tsv` có ít nhất hai địa chỉ khác nhau hay không, và in ra cảnh báo khi chỉ có một.

Is the `omp-rpc` DISTRIBUTION name being renamed at all? This blocks the item and the plan leaves it open. The stated default is KEEP `omp-rpc` permanently, on the grounds that renaming breaks every existing `pip install omp-rpc`. If that default stands, then `python/omp-rpc/pyproject.toml:6` stays AND `python/robomp/pyproject.toml:22` must stay as a coupled consequence, AND `Dockerfile:164`'s `pip install /tmp/wheels/omp_rpc-*.whl` keeps resolving. If the answer is instead to rename, this item grows a release-ordering requirement (publish the new name before retiring the old) and needs a changelog note in that package — which AGENTS.md forbids writing unless explicitly asked. The conservative default is assumed throughout this spec, and it is the only assumption that leaves the tree installable.

Is the `robomp` DISTRIBUTION name being renamed? The plan's open-questions table asks only about `omp-rpc` and says nothing about `robomp`, yet `python/robomp/pyproject.toml:6` is the same class of decision — a published PyPI name where renaming breaks every existing install. This spec assumes KEEP, but the question is genuinely unasked rather than answered, and `robomp` also encodes the old brand ('robo' + 'omp') in a way `omp-rpc` does not.

What is the new domain, and does `python/omp-rpc/pyproject.toml:26` move with it? `Homepage = "https://omp.sh/"` is the same value as `APP_URL` at `packages/utils/src/dirs.ts:24`, which the risk table freezes until a new domain actually resolves. If N9 has not been decided by the time this item lands, `:26` must be left alone rather than renamed on a guess. The safe default here is to leave it and record why.

Are `python/omp-rpc/pyproject.toml:27,28` (`Repository` and `Documentation`, both `https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi`) in scope for any milestone? They carry the old org name but are invisible to `git grep -n 'omp'`, because the string `oh-my-pi` does not contain the substring `omp`. W7 targets `@oh-my-pi/` with a trailing slash and would not match them; W8a handles bare `"oh-my-pi"` in TypeScript. A URL in a Python manifest currently belongs to nobody. Default: leave them, and do not let a W7 pass reach them by accident.

Does robomp's staged agent home need migrating when W6 flips `CONFIG_DIR_NAME`? `worker.py:145,168,209` and `entrypoint.sh:60,61,65,66,77-81` manage `/srv/agent-home/.omp` — the CLI's own config dir. This spec keeps them on `.omp` because W4's dual-root reader still reads the legacy root, which makes the current arrangement correct during the transition. But if `config migrate` (W5) has run on a container's volume, the staged home becomes stale and robomp would populate a root nobody reads. Nobody currently owns that hand-off. Default: keep as-is and raise it at W6; the fix is not safe to make before W4's dual-root reader is proven.
